ticker: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant on generators after power loss
Explosions reported in southern Iran amid escalating tensions
Saudi Aramco building damaged by falling debris in Riyadh
Delhi ranks as world's most polluted major city ahead of Diwali
US military launches task force to restrict Iranian land commerce

articles.headline: Zaporizhzhia plant relies on backup generators following power cut
articles.brief: The Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant is once again relying on emergency diesel generators after losing its external power supply, raising fresh nuclear safety concerns amid ongoing regional conflict.

articles.headline: Explosions reported across southern Iran according to local media
articles.brief: Multiple explosions have been heard in various areas across southern Iran, according to state and local media reports, as regional tensions continue to escalate sharply.

articles.headline: US military establishes new task force targeting Iranian land trade
articles.brief: Expanding beyond the existing naval blockade, the United States military has launched a specialized task force aimed at restricting Iranian land commerce and supply routes.

articles.headline: Democratic wins in state AG races challenge Trump agenda
articles.brief: Incoming Democratic state attorneys general are preparing to halt cooperation with federal immigration operations, fortify abortion access, and file multistate legal challenges against upcoming Trump administration policies.

articles.headline: Delhi ranks as world's most polluted major city ahead of Diwali
articles.brief: A Swiss group analysis has identified Delhi as the world's most polluted major city on the eve of the Diwali festival, amid growing air quality concerns.

articles.headline: Nearly 100 fall ill after consuming street food in Uttar Pradesh
articles.brief: Roughly 100 residents in Siddharthnagar village fell ill with vomiting and severe diarrhea after consuming contaminated pani puri and tikki from a local street vendor, prompting local health department interventions.

articles.headline: Microsoft employees describe work as joyless amid buyout offers
articles.brief: Thousands of Microsoft employees have signed an open letter criticizing the company's aggressive AI strategy at the expense of culture, coinciding with massive global buyout offers extended to 60,000 staff members.

articles.headline: Tesla to add Cybertruck production shift ahead of line closure
articles.brief: Tesla plans to introduce an additional Cybertruck shift in order to clear existing customer orders before permanently dismantling the manufacturing line next year.

articles.headline: India's ONGC targets operational rights for two Venezuelan oil fields
articles.brief: State-run Indian oil firm ONGC expects to secure rights to operate two major Venezuelan oil projects within the next six months following recent regulatory adjustments.

articles.headline: Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh damaged following attempted attack
articles.brief: A Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh sustained minor structural damage and shattered glass from falling debris following an attempted missile and aerial attack intercepted by civil defense forces.

articles.headline: Reserve Bank of India rejects rumors of new cheque book rules
articles.brief: The Reserve Bank of India has officially dismissed circulating rumors, clarifying that no new nationwide cheque book validation rules or formats will become effective in January.

articles.headline: Consumer court penalizes Karnataka society over unfulfilled fixed deposit
articles.brief: A consumer disputes redressal forum has ordered a Karnataka financial cooperative society to pay Rs 17.63 lakh to a depositor after the institution failed to return funds promised with high interest upon maturity.

articles.headline: Pakistan U-19 cricket team suffers embarrassing fielding blunder
articles.brief: Pakistan's youth cricket team went viral during the U-19 Asia Cup after three fielders collided and failed to catch a high-ball, gifting India an easy passage of play during a crucial group encounter.

articles.headline: Rinku Singh appointed India A vice-captain for Rising Stars Asia Cup
articles.brief: Hard-hitting batsman Rinku Singh has been named vice-captain of the India A squad for the upcoming Rising Stars Asia Cup following Rajat Patidar's withdrawal from the tournament.

articles.headline: Federal judge orders probe into illegal tree cutting at Trump golf course
articles.brief: A federal judge has appointed a former prosecutor to investigate whether government lawyers misled the court regarding the unapproved felling of over 400 trees at Donald Trump's Washington-area golf course.

articles.headline: JNU student arrested for attempted murder following campus assault
articles.brief: Delhi Police arrested a Jawaharlal Nehru University student for allegedly attempting to murder a fellow peer with multiple weapon strikes inside campus premises following a personal dispute.
